title: Welcome to Mind
subtitle: A guided tour of your second brain
description: An interactive walkthrough of the Mind app: open it, land on the Mind Home dashboard, and meet each of the 16 memory windows — people, teams, projects, meetings, decisions, incidents, action items, wins, competencies, evidence, reviews, goals, topics, patterns, gotchas and notes — learning what each holds and how they link into one knowledge graph.

steps.title: Welcome to Mind
steps.body:
**Mind** is your second brain — persistent memory that survives across AI sessions. It holds the people, projects, decisions, wins and lessons of your work, and every record links to the others, so the **graph builds itself**.

Let's open it and walk through each kind of memory. Use **Next** to step along, or **Esc** to leave anytime.

steps.title: Open your menu
steps.body: Navigation always starts from the **Menu** button on the left. Click it to open your menu — I'll continue the moment it opens.

steps.title: The Apps section
steps.body: Your menu has two halves — **Desktops**, your personal workspaces, and **Apps**, every installed application. This is the **Apps** section, and **Mind** lives here.

steps.title: Open the Mind app
steps.body: Click **Mind** to open it. Opening an app drops you straight onto its **home dashboard** — Mind Home. I'll continue once it loads.

steps.title: Mind Home
steps.body: This is **Mind Home** — now the background of your desktop. Each tile is a live window onto one kind of memory. There are sixteen; let's look at them one at a time.

steps.title: People
steps.body: **People** lists the `memory_people` collection — everyone you work with: colleagues, stakeholders, contacts. Most other records point back here, so a decision or a meeting also remembers who was part of it.

steps.title: Projects
steps.body: **Projects** lists the `memory_projects` collection — the initiatives you're involved in. They're the spine of the graph: meetings, decisions, action items, wins and incidents all link to the project they belong to.

steps.title: Meetings
steps.body: **Meetings** lists the `memory_meetings` collection — who met, when, and what came out of it. Link the attendees and the project and a meeting becomes a searchable point in your timeline, not a lost calendar entry.

steps.title: Wins
steps.body: **Wins** lists the `memory_wins` collection — the things that went well: shipped features, solved problems, good calls. Tie each to the competencies it shows and you've got ready-made evidence for your next review.

steps.title: Decisions
steps.body: **Decisions** lists the `memory_decisions` collection — the choices you made and, crucially, why. Months later, when someone asks why we did it this way, the reasoning is right here instead of lost to memory.

steps.title: Action Items
steps.body: **Action Items** lists the `memory_action_items` collection — the follow-ups that fall out of meetings, decisions and incidents. Each links back to where it came from, so nothing gets orphaned.

steps.title: Notes
steps.body: **Notes** lists the `memory_notes` collection — the free-form catch-all for anything that doesn't fit a tidier box yet. The markdown body is the content; add a person or project and even a loose note joins the graph.

steps.title: Goals
steps.body: **Goals** lists the `memory_goals` collection — what you're working toward: quarterly objectives, growth targets, personal aims. The wins, projects and competencies pointing at a goal tell its progress.

steps.title: Incidents
steps.body: **Incidents** lists the `memory_incidents` collection — when things went wrong: outages, breakages, mistakes. Capturing the what and the fix turns a bad day into a durable lesson, often spawning action items and gotchas.

steps.title: Evidence
steps.body: **Evidence** lists the `memory_evidence` collection — the proof behind your story: links, artifacts, metrics, quotes. It backs up competencies and reviews so claims about your impact aren't just assertions.

steps.title: Competencies
steps.body: **Competencies** lists the `memory_competencies` collection — the skills you're building and demonstrating. Wins and evidence link in as proof, and reviews assess them: this is where your growth is tracked over time.

steps.title: Reviews
steps.body: **Reviews** lists the `memory_reviews` collection — your performance reviews and retrospectives. They cite the competencies assessed and the evidence behind them, so a review writes itself from the graph you've built.

steps.title: Topics
steps.body: **Topics** lists the `memory_topics` collection — the subjects and areas of knowledge you care about. Use them to group notes, patterns and gotchas around a theme so related learnings cluster.

steps.title: Patterns
steps.body: **Patterns** lists the `memory_patterns` collection — the recurring shapes you've noticed: approaches that keep working, situations that keep repeating. Name a pattern once and reuse the insight everywhere it applies.

steps.title: Gotchas
steps.body: **Gotchas** lists the `memory_gotchas` collection — the traps learned the hard way: surprising footguns and edge cases. Write one down and you, or your AI, never get caught by it twice.

steps.title: Teams
steps.body: **Teams** lists the `memory_teams` collection — the groups people belong to. Link a person to their team and a project to the teams behind it, and you can see the human structure around any piece of work.

steps.title: That's your second brain!
steps.body:
You've met all sixteen kinds of memory — **people**, **teams** and **projects**; the work itself in **meetings**, **decisions**, **action items**, **incidents** and **wins**; your growth in **competencies**, **evidence**, **reviews** and **goals**; and your knowledge in **notes**, **topics**, **patterns** and **gotchas**.

The magic is the **links between them** — fill in the refs and the graph builds itself. Just talk to your AI as you work, and Mind remembers. Check the **Help Center** anytime.
